criteria: Does the Puppeteer PDF Worker node have explicit concurrency limits mapped to Kubernetes CPU/Memory requests to prevent node death during End of Month bursts?
hint: Define the max concurrent Headless Chrome sessions the worker node should accept.
placeholder: e.g., Limit concurrent PDF generations to 5 sessions per Pod with a 2GB RAM strict ceiling.

references.info: Puppeteer is extremely resource-heavy and causes Node.js OOM easily on Shared nodes.
references.source: System Context Information.md (Component Registry - Component 8: Puppeteer PDF Worker)

additional_info: We need to ensure EoM (End of Month) traffic spikes don't crash the adjoining microservices across the K8s cluster.

criteria: Are there automated Data Lifecycle Management (TTL) policies established on the AWS S3 exports bucket to strictly minimize long-term blob storage costs?
hint: Confirm if S3 objects have an explicit lifecycle rule configured to auto-delete after 24h.
placeholder: e.g., S3 Bucket policy enforces auto-deletion of objects tagged 'temporary_export' exactly after 24 hours.

references.info: Objects like PDF/CSV snapshosts are only valuable temporarily before they leak or escalate storage costs.
references.source: System Context Information.md (Component Registry - Component 9: AWS S3 Object Storage)

additional_info: GDPR/Compliance requires us not to store sensitive report data indefinitely if it's considered localized snapshot data.

criteria: Is there a strictly defined Rate-Limiting or Throttling policy applied directly to the NestJS Gateway routing tier?
hint: Provide explicit Throttler limits for the public Gateway endpoints (especially fetching and SSE mappings).
placeholder: e.g., Apply ThrottlerModule overriding max 20 req/sec per IP address natively in NestJS.

references.info: Monolithic backend exposed natively can easily be subjected to Thundering Herd attacks scaling out via SSE streams.
references.source: System Context Information.md (Component Registry - Component 2: NestJS REST API Gateway)

additional_info: Absolute necessity before lifting out of Local Staging into active Production channels.

criteria: Does the NestJS Background Cron Poller possess a robust Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) or fallback circuit-breaker mechanism if the External CRM throws HTTP 503?
hint: Outline how the integration safely stalls sync routines without crashing the Node event loop if the endpoint timeouts.
placeholder: e.g., Implementing Axios interceptors with a 3-retry backing-off algorithm before sliding into hibernation.

references.info: Synchronizing CRM delta records every 5 minutes puts hard dependency on External CRM SLA.
references.source: System Context Information.md (Component Registry - Component 3 & 7: Cron Poller / CRM Integration)

additional_info: Prevents cascading failures (Thread Starvation) within our own backend.
